tasks.spec:
You are an Elixir/OTP engineer finishing a port of the `run` command of Ringer (a Python agent-swarm CLI) to Cornerman (its Elixir/OTP port). A bakeoff produced a winning implementation, but it was built on an older commit. Your job: carry that implementation onto the current tree, fix the one behaviour it still gets wrong, and tidy three things a code review found. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the Cornerman repo at the current trunk. Edit files here directly.

NEVER TOUCH: anything under test/ (the conformance tests are the acceptance check), DIVERGENCES.toml, bin/, mix.exs, mix.lock, vendor/, .git. Do not git commit, push or git add. Add no dependencies.

OWNED PATHS: anything under lib/cornerman/, plus ./notes.md.

STEP 1: CARRY THE WINNING PATCH OVER. The patch is /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/swarms/phase2a/out/claude-opus/phase2a.patch (made against commit ee2f4a1; its author's notes, which explain the design, are /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/swarms/phase2a/out/claude-opus/notes.md). Apply it with `git apply --3way /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/swarms/phase2a/out/claude-opus/phase2a.patch` and resolve every conflict. Since ee2f4a1, trunk gained ten commits of lint-parity work (`git log --stat ee2f4a1..HEAD -- lib` and `git diff ee2f4a1 HEAD -- lib` show them). They changed APIs the patch calls, and the merged code will compile but fail at runtime unless you adapt it:
- Cornerman.Py.resolve and Cornerman.Py.expanduser now return {:ok, value} | {:error, message} (a `~user` whose home can't be found is an error, as in Python). Adapt every call site the patch adds or changes; an error becomes the same `cornerman: error: ...` exit 2 Python gives.
- Cornerman.Lint.findings now returns {:ok, findings} | {:error, message}, and the CLI prints findings through a printer that stops at the first line that can't be encoded (as Python's print raises). `run` must print its lint findings the same way lint does.
- lib/cornerman/cli/args.ex was rebuilt on a new Cornerman.CLI.Argparse module that ports argparse's option/value rules. Re-implement the patch's `run` subparser (manifest, --config, --max-parallel, --identity, --no-dashboard, --browser, --no-artifact, --dry-run, --allow-noncanonical-route; plus the global --config) on top of it.
- Manifest JSON now decodes through Cornerman.Py.Json (NaN/Infinity, insertion-ordered Py.Dict objects). Keep using the manifest structs, not raw maps.
- lib/cornerman/spawn/run.ex gained a fix on trunk (commit 711cceb: the leader's exit is matched only from erlexec's lwp pid). The patch made the same change and also added a respawn guard for exec-port's rare pre-exec "Cannot set effective group to 0" setpgid failure. Keep trunk's fix and the guard, and make sure the phase 0 spawn tests in test/cornerman/spawn_test.exs stay green.

STEP 2: FIX THE FAILING CASE `run/background-child-holds-stdout` in test/conformance/run_test.exs. A worker that starts a background child and exits: Ringer keeps reading the worker's stdout until EOF, for at most 5 seconds after the worker exits (ringer.py _run_worker at 9207-9223: `await asyncio.wait_for(reader, timeout=5)`, then cancel), so output the child writes in that window reaches the log, the capture tail and the CLI's stdout, and the verifier only starts after that. The patch reports the exit as soon as the leader exits and drops the rest. Match Ringer: keep relaying output after the leader's exit until the pipe closes or 5 s have passed, then carry on. Do this without leaking the child: if the window expires the child's output is simply no longer read (Ringer does not kill it there).

STEP 3: THREE REVIEW FINDINGS.
(a) A crash inside one task's lifecycle aborts the run with exit 2 and no summary, and leaves the state JSON unfinished. Ringer, when an unexpected exception escapes a task: RingerRunner.run's finally block still stops the state writer, prints the summary and the closing lines, and main then prints `ringer.py: error: <message>` and exits 2. Make Cornerman do the same (summary and closing lines printed, state flushed, then `cornerman: error: <message>` and exit 2), and never leave a worker process group running.
(b) Worker output is sent to the CLI process chunk by chunk with no backpressure, so a flood of output while stdout is slow grows the CLI's mailbox without bound. Make delivery to the output sink synchronous (the lifecycle waits for the write), keeping the bytes and their order unchanged.
(c) TaskLifecycle is about 650 lines and mixes the state machine with harvest, token/model parsing and deliverable handling. Move those into their own modules so the gen_statem reads as the state machine; keep the explicit verifying -> running retry transition inside it.

DESIGN RULES (unchanged from the bakeoff): the run subtree stays host-agnostic (phase 3 hosts it in a daemon): no System.halt and no terminal writes inside it except through the sink the CLI gives it. Tasks are :gen_statem processes, restart :temporary; domain retries are explicit transitions, never supervisor restarts; timeouts are gen_statem timeouts; OS processes only through Cornerman.Spawn; Phoenix.PubSub events with StateMirror and EvalLog as subscribers; atomic temp-file-plus-rename writes; validated structs at the boundary. Data-plane strings stay byte-identical to Ringer (`[ringer.py]` log markers, shepherd_model "none (ringer.py)", pattern "ringer-py"); only CLI text a human reads says `cornerman`.

SETUP (run once, first, from this directory; the sandbox cannot fetch packages and this worktree has no submodule checkout):
  cp -R /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/deps ./deps
  export PATH=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/elixir/1.20.1-otp-28/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/erlang/28.5/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin:$PATH HEX_OFFLINE=1 CORNERMAN_ORACLE=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py CORNERMAN_PYTHON=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3

HOW TO RUN (after the setup, from this directory):
  MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format
  mix test                                               # everything: lint, run, spawn. Must pass in full.
  mix test test/conformance/run_test.exs:<line>          # one case; a failure names the field or file that differs
  CORNERMAN_SELF_CHECK=1 mix test test/conformance/run_test.exs   # oracle vs oracle: proves the harness, always passes
The verifying check (it must finish within Ringer's 60 s) runs a smoke subset outside your sandbox: owned paths, format, compile, the background-child case and a spread of run and lint cases. The orchestrator then runs the whole suite twice from clean dependencies and fails the lane if any case fails, so make `mix test` pass in full yourself before you stop.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the change under lib/cornerman/, formatted, compiling with no warnings, plus ./notes.md with: every conflict and API break you resolved and how, how the post-exit read window works, how a task crash now flows to the summary and exit 2, the module split, the final `mix test` result line, anything your sandboxed run could not exercise, and any conformance case you believe is wrong, with the reason.
tasks.verified: the winning phase 2a patch is carried onto trunk: formatted, compiles without warnings, and the background-child case plus a spread of run and lint conformance cases match the oracle; the full suite runs twice in the orchestrator's gate afterwards.
